question: Does the 2014 embryonic-development paper provide a dated, site-resolved wild occurrence or independent species confirmation for Pterygoplichthys pardalis in Marikina River?

source.title: Embryonic and larval development of the suckermouth sailfin catfish Pterygoplichthys pardalis from Marikina River, Philippines
source.citation: Jumawan, J. C., Herrera, A. A., & Vallejo, B., Jr. (2014). Embryonic and larval development of the suckermouth sailfin catfish Pterygoplichthys pardalis from Marikina River, Philippines. EurAsian Journal of Biosciences, 8, 38–50. https://doi.org/10.5053/ejobios.2014.8.0.4
source.accessMethod: Checked the University of the Philippines Diliman IESM author bibliography and DOI metadata. The DOI redirects to the journal PDF, which the review browser could not retrieve; the author-uploaded ResearchGate full-text copy was reviewed for abstract, methods, results, acknowledgements, and references. No PDF, figure, table, photograph, or raw measurements were retained.
source.copyrightAndReuse: The article copy displays © EurAsian Journal of BioSciences. No item-specific Creative Commons license or separate reuse permission was identified in the reviewed material. This record summarizes citation and study scope only; it does not redistribute article text, tables, figures, photographs, or measurements.

studyDesign.waterbodyAsReported: Marikina River; the paper does not identify a collection station or reach within the river.
studyDesign.sourceReportedTaxon: Pterygoplichthys pardalis (Castelnau, 1855), as labeled by the article; not independently confirmed by voucher or sequence in the reviewed source.
studyDesign.collectionPeriod: July to September, described as the peak spawning months; no calendar year is stated.

fieldParentFish.localities: The river is named, but collection sites, barangays, stations, and individual capture localities are not given.
fieldParentFish.voucherOrAccession: No voucher catalogue numbers or genetic accessions were found in the reviewed full text.

studyDesign.experimentalDesign: Adult fish were collected from the field, and the study induced spawning in females using human chorionic gonadotropin, removed male testes for milt, and fertilized eggs in vitro. Embryos were incubated in laboratory aquaria, including a reported 1:1 Marikina River-water/tap-water medium in later trials. The developmental observations describe laboratory-reared eggs and young, not wild nests or a field larval survey.
studyDesign.findingsScope: The article reports fertilization, hatching, survival, embryogenesis, and yolk-resorption observations under its laboratory setup. These are experimental results and do not estimate river abundance, catch rate, natural recruitment, or current seasonal catchability.
studyDesign.interpretation: The 36 source-reported adult fish provide historical Marikina River research context, but the unknown year, unspecified reach, absent gear/effort, and unresolved Pterygoplichthys species boundary prevent a dated species occurrence or independent species confirmation.

related2010NastAbstract.relationship: The 2014 paper cites Jumawan, Herrera, and Jacinto (2010b) as a NAST Transactions item on Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus from Marikina River. This supports a related reproductive-research publication trail, but the 2014 paper gives no sample identifiers linking its 36 adults to that abstract.
related2010NastAbstract.decision: Treat the NAST abstract and 2014 developmental study as related publications with unresolved specimen overlap; do not combine their source-reported species labels or sample counts.

related2011MatrixModel.relationship: The model paper reports an undated 200-fish fecundity sample and cites a 2010 BAR proceedings item. The 2014 article cites a differently described 2010 NAST abstract. The bibliography entries are distinct, but whether the BAR contribution republishes or shares data with the NAST abstract is unresolved; no sample identifiers link either item to the 2014 sample.
related2011MatrixModel.decision: Do not merge the citations or equate the 36 parent fish with either the model paper’s 200 fish or the later 1,133 fish sample without a specimen-level crosswalk.

related2011BarcodeStudy.relationship: The 2011 COI study reports Marikina Pterygoplichthys samples and unresolved P. pardalis/P. disjunctivus boundaries. The 2014 article provides no voucher or accession that links its adults to the barcode series.
related2011BarcodeStudy.decision: Retain P. pardalis as the 2014 paper’s source label only; do not treat the COI study as identification evidence for these 36 fish.

related2016LifeHistoryStudy.relationship: The 2016 study reports July 2010–June 2011 sampling at five named stations. The 2014 paper gives only July–September without a year or station. Shared river and author context do not establish cohort overlap or independence.
related2016LifeHistoryStudy.decision: Do not assign the 2014 adults to the 2016 stations, calendar period, or aggregate sample.

publicationLineage.independenceDecision: The 2014 article is a laboratory developmental experiment using 36 field-collected adult fish, not a complete fish survey. Its specimen lineage relative to the 2010 NAST item, 2011 model and barcode samples, and 2016 life-history sample is unresolved.

related2010BarProceedingsCitation.relationship: The BAR contribution is cited in the 2011 matrix and barcode papers, while the 2014 paper cites the separate NAST abstract. Both 2010 references share authors and subject matter but differ in printed title, venue, and pages; the BAR primary item was not retrieved.
related2010BarProceedingsCitation.decision: Do not equate the 2014 adult-fish sample with the BAR or NAST material, and do not interpret the citation difference as proof of sample independence.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain as historical research-only Marikina River reproductive and developmental context. Keep the 36 adult parent fish, laboratory outputs, and source-reported P. pardalis label separate from occurrence data and other Marikina study cohorts.

nonClaims: The article’s P. pardalis label is not independently verified for these 36 fish by vouchers, diagnostic re-identification, or sequence accessions in the reviewed source.
July–September is the article’s stated collection/experimental season window, not a verified calendar year or a present-day fishing-season recommendation.
The 18 females and 18 males are laboratory-study parent fish, not a river population estimate, catch total, or standardized survey count.
The article does not state gear, field effort, collection stations, barangays, capture coordinates, or specimen identifiers.
Laboratory fertilization and incubation findings are not observations of natural spawning, wild egg/larval distribution, or river-wide recruitment.
No relationship or specimen overlap is established with the NAST abstract, the 2011 matrix-model sample, the 2011 COI series, or the 2016 five-station sample.
No current occurrence, abundance, catchability, diet, safety, legal access, geometry, fish image, or public app claim is derived from this review.
nextActions: Keep the paper in research-only status while NCR and CALABARZON freshwater coverage remains incomplete.
Resolve the source-reported species label only if diagnostic specimen evidence, a museum voucher, or an accession can be tied to these fish.
Do not treat the paper’s July–September window as current seasonality or allocate its adult sample to a river station.
